Tafsir of Surat al-Jinn

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger ﷺ to inform his people: that the jinn listened to the Qur'an, believed in it, affirmed it and submitted to it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened and said: Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct (rushd), so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.﴾ That is: to rectitude (sadad) and success. This situation is similar to His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We directed to you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29]. We have already presented the narrations related to that, in a manner that makes repeating them here unnecessary.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that He, exalted is the majesty (jadd) of our Lord﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿jadd of our Lord﴾, that is: His action, His command and His power.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: the jadd of Allah is His blessings, His power and His favour upon His creation.

It is related from Mujahid and 'Ikrimah: the majesty (jalal) of our Lord. Qatadah said: exalted is His majesty, His greatness and His command. Al-Suddi said: exalted is the command of our Lord. It is narrated from Abu al-Darda', Mujahid also, and Ibn Jurayj: exalted is His remembrance. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿exalted is the jadd of our Lord﴾, that is: exalted is our Lord.

As for what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' [[In M: "'Abd Allah ibn Suwayd al-Kufi".]] narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "al-jadd" is "father." And if the jinn had known that there is a jadd among mankind, they would not have said: "exalted is the jadd of our Lord."

This is a sound chain, but I do not understand the meaning of this statement; perhaps something has fallen out, and Allah knows best. His saying: ﴿He has not taken a companion or a son﴾, that is: exalted is He above taking a companion and children. That is, the jinn said, when they accepted Islam and believed in the Qur'an: exalted is the Lord, in His majesty and greatness, above taking a companion and a son.

Then they said: ﴿And that it was our foolish one who used to speak about Allah an excessive transgression (shatat)﴾. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿our foolish one﴾ means Iblis. ﴿Shatat﴾: al-Suddi narrated from Abu Malik: ﴿shatat﴾ means injustice. Ibn Zayd said: great wrongdoing.

It is possible that by their saying ﴿our foolish one﴾ is meant a collective noun for everyone who claims that Allah has a companion or a son. That is why they said: ﴿And that it was our foolish one who used to speak﴾, that is, before his becoming Muslim, ﴿about Allah an excessive transgression﴾, that is, falsehood and lies. ﴿And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak a lie against Allah﴾, that is: we did not think that mankind and the jinn would collude in lying against Allah by attributing to Him a companion and a son. So when we heard this Qur'an and believed in it, we knew that they had been lying against Allah in that.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾. That is: we used to see that we had superiority over mankind, because they would seek refuge with us, that is, when they descended into a valley or a desolate place of the wilderness and other places, as was the custom of the Arabs in their jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance). They would seek refuge with the greatest of that place from the jinn, that it might not harm them with anything that would distress them, just as one of them would enter the lands of his enemies under the protection, guarantee and safe-conduct of a great man. When the jinn saw that mankind sought refuge with them out of their fear of them, ﴿so they increased them in rahaq﴾, that is: fear, terror and dread, until they became even more fearful of them and more intensely seeking refuge with them. As Qatadah said: ﴿so they increased them in rahaq﴾, that is: sin. And the jinn became bolder against them because of that.

al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿so they increased them in rahaq﴾, that is: the jinn became bolder against them.

Al-Suddi said: a man would go out with his family, come to the land, descend upon it and say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the jinn, that I or my property or my children or my livestock may be harmed." He said: when he sought refuge with them besides Allah, the jinn then overwhelmed them with harm.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah who said: The jinn used to fear mankind just as mankind feared them, or more. And when mankind descended into a valley, the jinn would flee. The chief of the people would say: "We seek refuge with the lord of the people of this valley."

Then the jinn said: "We see them fearing us just as we fear them." So they approached mankind and afflicted them with madness and insanity. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿rahaq﴾ means fear. al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿so they increased them in rahaq﴾, that is: sin. Qatadah said likewise. Mujahid said: the disbelievers increased in transgression.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Farwah ibn al-Maghra' al-Kindi narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn Malik (i.e., al-Muzani) narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from his father, from Kardam ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Ansari who said: I went out with my father from Medina on some errand, and that was when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was first mentioned in Mecca. Night overtook us at the dwelling of a shepherd of sheep. When midnight came, a wolf came and seized a lamb from the sheep. The shepherd leapt up and said: "O Amir of the valley, protect your neighbour!" Then a caller we could not see called out: "O Sirhan, release it!" So the lamb came running until it entered among the sheep, and it was not harmed in the slightest. And Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Messenger in Mecca: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in rahaq﴾.

Then he said: It is also narrated from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, something similar.

It may be that this wolf which seized the lamb, which is the young of the sheep, was a jinni, so as to frighten the human and make him fear it, then returned it to him when he sought its protection, in order to mislead him, humiliate him, and take him out of his religion. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And that they thought, just as you thought, that Allah would never raise up any messenger﴾, that is: Allah would not send a messenger after this period. This was said by al-Kalbi and Ibn Jarir.

Part of His preservation of the Qur'an was that the sky was filled with a severe guard, it was protected from all its regions, and the devils were driven away from the seats they used to occupy before that, so that they would not steal anything of the Qur'an and convey it to the tongues of the soothsayers (kahin). The matter would then become confused and mixed up, and no one would know who was truthful. This was from Allah's kindness to His creation, His mercy to His servants, and His preservation of His Mighty Book.

For this reason the jinn said: ﴿And we touched the sky, but found it filled with a severe guard and flaming meteors. And we used to sit in it on certain seats to listen. This is from their courtesy in speech, for they attributed evil to no agent, and they attributed good to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It has been reported in the Sahih (the authentic collection of hadith): "And evil is not attributed to You." Stars had been hurled before that, but not frequently; rather, only at certain times and occasionally. This is as in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas [in another copy: "as in the hadith of al-'Abbas"]: "While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a star was hurled and it lit up. They began to traverse the eastern and western regions of the earth, and they found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ leading his companions in prayer. Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 72, verses 25–28:

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to the people: "Indeed, he has no knowledge of the time of the Hour, and he does not know whether its time is near or far." ﴿Say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a long term.﴾ That is: a long period.

In this noble verse is evidence that the report circulated by many ignorant people, that he (ﷺ) would not compile (a book) under the earth, is a lie with no basis, and we have not found it in any of the books. He (ﷺ) was asked about the time of the Hour and he did not answer about it. When Jibril appeared to him in the form of a Bedouin, among what he asked was: "O Muhammad, inform me about the Hour?" He said: "The one asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the asker." [[This is part of the long hadith of Jibril, narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (8), from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.]] When that Bedouin called out to him in a loud voice, saying: "O Muhammad, when is the Hour?" He said: "Woe to you! It is certainly coming, so what have you prepared for it?" He said: "As for me, I have not prepared much [[In M: "kabir" (great).]] prayer or fasting, but I love Allah and His Messenger." He said: "You will be with whom you love." Anas said: "The Muslims never rejoiced at anything as they rejoiced at this hadith." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2639), from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

By the One in whose hand is my soul, what you are promised is surely coming." [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (10564), by way of al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, with the same chain.]]

Abu Dawud said at the end of the "Kitab al-Malahim" (Book of Great Battles): Musa ibn Suhayl narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will not make this nation fail (to be brought to account) after half a day." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4349). Also narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/424) by way of Ibn Wahb, with the same wording. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of both (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it."]] Abu Dawud alone narrated it. Then Abu Dawud said:

Amr ibn 'Uthman narrated to us. Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, Safwan narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "I truly hope that my nation will not fail before its Lord, that He will delay them by half a day." It was said to Sa'd: "And how long is half a day?" He said: "Five hundred years." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4350). Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd did not meet Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, so the chain is disconnected (munqati').]]

As for His saying: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger He has approved﴾, this is like His saying: ﴿They do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255]. Likewise, here He states that He knows the unseen and the seen, and that none of His creation is informed of any part of His knowledge except what Allah, exalted is He, makes them aware of. For this reason He said: ﴿He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger He has approved﴾, and this includes both the angelic messenger and the human messenger.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards [rasad]﴾, that is: He singles him out with additional attendant angels [mu'aqqibat] (angels who follow in succession) who protect him from the command of Allah and accompany him with what he carries of the revelation of Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompasses what is with them and has enumerated everything in number.﴾

The exegetes have differed about the pronoun in His saying ﴿That He may know [liya'lama]﴾, to what it refers. It was said that it refers to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi [[In A: "al-'Ami."]] narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger He has approved. Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards﴾, he said: "Four guardians from the angels are with Jibril, ﴿that he [Muhammad (ﷺ)] may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompasses what is with them and has enumerated everything in number.﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through the hadith of Ya'qub al-Qummi [[In A: "al-'Ami."]] with the same chain. Likewise it was narrated by al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Yazid ibn Abi Habib.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾, he said: "That the Prophet of Allah may know that the messengers have conveyed from Allah, and that the angels preserved it and warded off (harm) from it." Likewise it was narrated by Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose this view.
